premise_correction_note.note: The contract's central claim was overstated and its author's follow-up hypothesis was wrong. scope.summary: Make the in-crate cfg(test) modules in api/flight_recorder.rs and workflows.rs run against a live embedded SurrealDB store instead of a store that has already been shut down, and delete the vestigial skip branches that can no longer be taken. Today both modules build, but their setup_state helpers destroy the store before the first assertion runs.
scope.defect: Both helpers are declared to return Result<Option<AppState>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>. Each calls embedded_test_backend, moves the database and storage fields into the AppState, and then lets the partially-moved EmbeddedTestBackend fall out of scope at the end of the function. EmbeddedTestBackend carries a private cleanup field holding an Arc<TestStoreCleanupGuard> whose Drop shuts the store down and removes its data directory, and the Arc strong count is 1 at that point, so the shutdown always runs. Every test that then touches storage gets the embedded-database-is-closed error. This is the exact failure MT-144 diagnosed and fixed in the other five modules by returning the backend alongside the state and binding it so it outlives the test body.
scope.secondary_defect: Both helpers still return an Option and always return Some, a shape left over from the PostgreSQL era when the backend could legitimately be absent. 28 call sites in api/flight_recorder.rs and 26 in workflows.rs still open with a let-else that returns Ok early when the state is None, so each of those 54 tests carries a silent-skip branch that can never be taken. The branch is dead today, but it is the same construct that let 17 tests pass while proving nothing before MT-144 removed it.
scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. No SQLite and no PostgreSQL may be added, restored, imported, or referenced as a live backend. Historical mentions in doc comments that explain why a skip branch was removed are permitted, matching the convention already used in storage/tests.rs and accepted for MT-144.
acceptance_criteria: AC-145-1: setup_state in both modules returns the EmbeddedTestBackend alongside the AppState so the store outlives every assertion, using the same tuple shape MT-144 established.

AC-145-2: every let-else skip call site becomes an unconditional binding that also holds the backend for the life of the test. The count is 55, not the 54 this contract first stated: api/flight_recorder.rs has 28 `let Some(state)` plus one `let Some(base_state)` at line 2982, and workflows.rs has 26. No test keeps a branch that can return Ok without asserting anything.

AC-145-3: no assertion is weakened, ignored, or deleted to make a test pass. Every test that fails once the store is live must be either fixed or recorded with a named owner and a stated reason; none may be quietly marked ignore.
AC-145-4: the full api::flight_recorder and workflows in-crate suites are run and their pass and fail counts recorded verbatim, including a per-test attribution for every failure.

AC-145-5: no SQLite or PostgreSQL identifier, DSN, env var, or helper survives as live code INSIDE THE cfg(test) MODULES this microtask touches. Live product references elsewhere in workflows.rs are explicitly out of scope and must not be touched: an error string at line 2909 and a real call to locus::sqlite_store::parse_locus_operation at line 11034 are working product behaviour, not test-era leftovers.
AC-145-6: the product binary still builds, proving the change stayed inside cfg(test).
proof_targets: PT-145-1: a RED capture taken BEFORE the fix showing at least one test in each module failing with the embedded-database-is-closed error, so the defect is demonstrated rather than asserted.
PT-145-2: the api::flight_recorder in-crate suite run to completion with counts recorded.
PT-145-3: the workflows in-crate suite run to completion with counts recorded.
PT-145-4: the product binary build still succeeds.
execution_constraints: CARGO_TARGET_DIR must be an owner-scoped child of ../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target/ with a SHORT slug. Bundled DuckDB C++ headers hit the MSVC 260-character path limit and fail with C1083 if the target path is long; enabling long paths in the registry does not help cl.exe.
HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT must be set to the absolute artifacts root or embedded_test_backend refuses to start.
Each test opens its own RocksDB store, so a 28-test module takes roughly 30 minutes. Budget for that rather than assuming a hang.
Do not touch src/backend/handshake_core/tests/**: MT-141 owns that tree.
Do not touch api/memory.rs: its three remaining assertion failures are owned by MT-146.
scope.risk_if_missed: 43 of the 55 in-crate tests in these two modules touch the store after setup_state and therefore fail deterministically with Database("embedded database is closed") the moment they are actually run; they currently compile and are counted as present while proving nothing. The remaining 12 never touch the store and would pass either way, but they still carry a skip branch that can never be taken — the same construct that let 17 tests pass while proving nothing before MT-144 removed it. Left unfixed, any of the 43 that is expected to guard flight-recorder ingestion or workflow execution against regression is providing no protection at all.

defects_found_during_implementation.source: Reported by the implementing agent after reading the source rather than the brief, and independently verified by the orchestrator against workflows.rs before amending this contract.

items.finding: The call-site count is 55, not 54. api/flight_recorder.rs carries a 29th instance in the form of `let Some(base_state)` at line 2982, which the original count missed because it only matched `let Some(state)`.

workflows.rs contains a 56th instance of the same store-lifetime defect outside setup_state: fems_forget_persists_exact_status_events_and_sorted_commit_hash at roughly line 30470 calls embedded_test_backend() inline and moves both fields out of the returned backend. It compiles in this feature set because app-runtime enables duckdb-flight-recorder.
items.disposition: In scope: it is in an allowed path and is the same defect this microtask exists to remove. Fix it and disclose it rather than leaving one instance of the class behind.

items.finding: AC-145-5 as originally written was not satisfiable without violating AC-145-6. It demanded that no SQLite identifier survive as live code in either module, but workflows.rs carries two live product references: an error string at line 2909 and a call to locus::sqlite_store::parse_locus_operation at line 11034 inside the job dispatcher. Both are working product behaviour, not test-era residue, and removing them would be a product-code change in a contract whose own criterion requires the change to stay inside cfg(test).
items.disposition: Contract defect, mine. AC-145-5 is narrowed to the cfg(test) surface and the two live references are named as explicitly out of scope. The implementer was right to refuse to either touch live code or claim the module clean.
items.author_note: The criterion was copied from MT-144, where every affected module was a test-only surface. workflows.rs is not, and the criterion should not have been carried across unchanged.

premise_correction_2026_09_04.retracted_claim: The original risk_if_missed said 54 in-crate tests 'cannot exercise storage at all'. That is wrong in two separate ways and is retracted here rather than quietly worked around in the implementation.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.error_1_overcounted: 12 of the 55 tests never touch the store after setup_state returns, so the store's lifetime is irrelevant to them and they would pass either way. api::flight_recorder has 11 such tests (its 29 setup_state tests break down as 18 that touch the store — 8 directly and 10 through a helper — and 11 that do not); workflows has 1 (25 of its 26 touch the store directly). The honest number of tests losing real proof is 43, not 54. The fix is still correct for all 55 because it deletes the dead skip branch from every one of them, but those 12 must not be counted as tests whose proof was destroyed.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.error_2_mischaracterised_mechanism: I then hypothesised, from a green RED, that the defect was racy — that the store was mid-teardown and tests passed or failed on timing. The implementer refuted that with measurement and was right. The behaviour is deterministic: the store handle is closed before the test body runs, so the first storage call returns Database("embedded database is closed") every time. What the discriminator actually is: whether the test touches the store after setup_state, not when it does so.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.why_the_first_red_was_green: The implementer's initial RED target, list_events_preserves_model_session_id_filter_and_payload, is one of the 11 flight_recorder tests that never touch the store — it uses only the in-memory DuckDB recorder. It was chosen because it was the first call site in the file. That is a measurement error in target selection, not evidence that the defect is absent, and the implementer identified it as its own error before I did.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.the_30_second_timeout_is_a_different_def: The 'shutdown failed: still draining operations after 30000 ms' line appears in BOTH the passing and the failing run, so it is a constant and not what separates them. Two distinct things are happening: the handle close takes effect immediately, which is what fails the storage-touching tests; the directory REMOVAL separately times out after 30 seconds and leaves the store on disk with os error 32. The latter is the MT-123 teardown defect, already disclosed there, and is unrelated to this microtask. Do not conflate them.
premise_correction_2026_09_04.incidental_cost_finding: TestStoreCleanupGuard::drop spawns a cleanup thread and joins it, so setup_state blocks up to 30 seconds on a shutdown that then times out anyway. Every one of these 55 tests pays that stall, which is roughly half an hour of pure teardown wait across the two modules and partly explains why a single test can run for 417 seconds. Recorded as an observation for whoever owns MT-123; not in scope here.
evidence: Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp-kernel-012-kb-0902-proof-logs/red2-workflows.log - model_run_timeout_ms_fails_before_simulated_runtime_finishes FAILED with Error: Database("embedded database is closed"), 0 passed 1 failed

The implementer committed to reporting a green result as falsifying the deterministic reading rather than trying another target.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend test-only harness repair with no operator-visible or model-navigable surface.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: No product behaviour, tool, command, config key, IPC channel, or navigation path changes; the work is confined to cfg(test) code.

risks: Reaching green by re-adding a skip branch or an ignore attribute, which converts a visible failure back into a silent pass and recreates the exact condition this contract exists to remove.
Binding the returned backend to a bare underscore, which drops it immediately and reintroduces the defect while looking like the fix.
Tests that have never actually run against storage may fail for real once the store is live; treating those as breakage caused by this change and weakening the assertion to compensate.
Replacing a real storage assertion with a mock so the test compiles and passes but proves nothing.
minimum_controls: PT-145-1 requires the RED to be captured before the fix, so the pre-existing state is on the record.
AC-145-3 requires every post-fix failure to carry a named owner and a stated reason rather than an ignore attribute.
AC-145-4 requires per-test attribution, not a summary count.
AC-145-6 proves the runtime binary is untouched.

hbr_obligations.INT: No observable runtime behaviour changes, so the HBR-INT-009 three-tier consideration is NOT_APPLICABLE. The change is confined to cfg(test) code.
hbr_obligations.VIS: NOT_APPLICABLE: no GUI, operator, diagnostic, or frontend surface is touched.
hbr_obligations.MAN: NOT_APPLICABLE per user_manual_obligation: no product behaviour, command, channel, config key, or navigation path changes.
hbr_obligations.QUIET: Compiles and test runs stay headless and must not foreground anything or steal focus.
hbr_obligations.STOP: No capacity, token, or session-count stop reasons. A test that genuinely cannot be made to pass is recorded with its owner and reason under AC-145-3, not silenced.
